findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex-wide lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index
findings.body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for its whole duration, which made a concurrent `GetIndex` (RLock) block until the build finished, so a second caller observed the finished index instead of starting its own build. Now the lock is only taken around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write, so two callers (e.g. the startup indexing goroutines in `searchSupport.init` and a watch event going through `getOrCreateIndex`) can both see `GetIndex == nil` for the same NamespacedResource and build in parallel. For file-based indexes this means two goroutines call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory (`Root/namespace/resource.group`), and the second one fails (path already exists) or corrupts the on-disk index; for memory indexes the work is duplicated and one index is silently dropped from the cache while documents may still be written to it. The duplicate-build window needs to be guarded per key (e.g. keyed mutex / singleflight) rather than removed entirely.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` now writes to that map from many concurrent goroutines (the lock was narrowed to just the map write). Concurrent map read + write causes a fatal `concurrent map read and map write` runtime panic. This path is newly exercised on every startup by the added log line in `searchSupport.init` (`s.search.TotalDocs()`), and can also be hit at any time if metrics/logging call it while a watch event triggers a lazy index build. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: init() goroutines write shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization
findings.body: Inside `group.Go(...)` the closures do `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)`, both of which mutate variables declared in the enclosing function from up to `initWorkers` goroutines running in parallel. This is a data race (detectable by `-race`, and the counter reported in the `namespaces indexed` span event can be wrong/undercounted), and assigning to the shared `err` instead of returning the value through the errgroup can also overwrite an error from another worker. Use a local `err :=` inside the closure (returning it) and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Stop()'s initErr is no longer surfaced; requests are served after shutdown
findings.body: All the per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return ... }` guards were removed, but `Stop()` still communicates shutdown exclusively by setting `s.initErr = "service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`. Since nothing reads `initErr` after construction anymore, calls arriving during or after shutdown no longer fail fast; they proceed against a backend whose lifecycle hooks have been stopped and whose watcher context has been cancelled, producing confusing internal errors instead of a clear "service is stopping" response. Either add an explicit closed/stopped check on the request paths or drop the now-dead initErr mutation in Stop().

findings.title: Context cancel func leaked when Init fails in NewResourceServer
findings.body: `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created a few lines above, and on the new `s.Init(ctx)` error path the function returns `nil, err` without ever calling `cancel()`. The cancel func is also only reachable through the discarded `server` value, so the derived context (and any timer/goroutine attached to it) is leaked for the lifetime of the process. Call `cancel()` before returning the error (also applies to the `newSearchSupport` error return just above).

findings.title: Index build now blocks server construction and makes startup fail hard
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now runs the full `Init` (lifecycle init + building every namespace's search index) synchronously before returning. Two consequences worth confirming: (1) process/DI startup is blocked for as long as indexing takes (the PR description says it can exceed a gRPC deadline, i.e. potentially minutes on large installs), so nothing else that depends on this constructor — including the HTTP server/readiness endpoint in single-binary mode — comes up during that time; (2) any transient failure during index build (DB hiccup, bleve directory error) now aborts construction and prevents the server from starting at all, whereas before only the failing request errored and a later request would retry `Init`. Consider doing the index build in the background with a readiness gate, or at least bounding it with a timeout and tolerating per-namespace failures.

findings.title: BuildIndex still discards the span context, breaking the trace fix for builder work
findings.body: The PR fixes trace propagation in `searchSupport.build` and `GetResourceStats` by assigning the derived context, but `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. The builder callback invoked at line 126 uses the context captured from `searchSupport.build`, so all storage/list spans produced during the actual index build are siblings of the `BuildIndex` span rather than children, and the BuildIndex span appears empty in traces. Propagate the derived context into `builder(idx)` (e.g. by making the builder accept a ctx or by assigning `ctx, span := ...`).

findings.title: Postgres integration coverage for the storage-server target is silently disabled
findings.body: `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` now skips whenever `GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres`, leaving only MySQL exercising the storage-server module path. Given this PR changes when unified storage initializes (now inside `NewResourceServer`, i.e. during module startup), postgres is exactly the configuration where a startup regression would go unnoticed. The skip reason ("works locally") suggests the test is actually failing with these changes in CI; the root cause should be understood before merging, and the TODO should reference a tracking issue so the coverage is restored.
